description: Execute a PartiQL statement. Supports SELECT (with LIMIT, nested paths), INSERT (with IF NOT EXISTS, parameter placeholders), UPDATE (with SET arithmetic, REMOVE, nested paths), DELETE. UPDATE and DELETE accept a RETURNING clause, surfaced in the response Items: DELETE allows only RETURNING ALL OLD * (returning the deleted item; other variants are rejected), UPDATE allows all four RETURNING <ALL|MODIFIED> <OLD|NEW> * variants. WHERE supports BETWEEN, IN, CONTAINS, IS MISSING, IS NOT MISSING, AND, OR, NOT, parenthesised grouping up to 64 levels deep, and nested paths; AND binds tighter than OR, and a NOT over a group is applied by De Morgan. An index is named in the FROM clause as "table"."index", which serves the read from that GSI or LSI on SELECT only; a write statement rejects the qualifier. An UPDATE or DELETE whose WHERE condition fails is a ConditionalCheckFailedException; with return_values_on_condition_check_failure set to ALL_OLD the error carries the item the condition was evaluated against. Write statements are blocked in read-only mode.

consistent_read.description: Whether to use strongly consistent reads. Does not change which rows come back, but it doubles the rate a SELECT is charged at and it makes a SELECT qualified by a GSI a rejection, because a GSI cannot serve one.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to evaluate for SELECT statements (not necessarily the number returned); a filtered page can come back short or empty and still carry a NextToken

next_token.description: Continuation token from a previous SELECT response, to fetch the next page. Pass back the NextToken the last call returned; its absence means there are no more pages. The statement must stay identical character for character across pages, and so must the parameters; a token replayed with any difference is rejected with a ValidationException. A statement with a list or map parameter cannot be paged past its first page, as on DynamoDB.

parameters.description: A JSON array of positional parameters in DynamoDB JSON, one for each ? in the statement, in order. For example, [{"S": "user#1"}, {"N": "42"}] for WHERE pk = ? AND n = ?.

return_consumed_capacity.description: What consumed capacity to return: TOTAL for the operation's total, INDEXES for the total broken down by table and index, or NONE (the default) for none. Figures follow DynamoDB's charging rules and match what the DynamoDB API returns for the same request.

return_values_on_condition_check_failure.description: What to return when an UPDATE or DELETE fails its WHERE condition: ALL_OLD hands back the item the condition was evaluated against as the error's item; NONE, the default, does not. Any other value is rejected with a ValidationException.

statement.description: PartiQL statement to execute. Supports SELECT (with LIMIT, nested path projections, and NextToken paging), INSERT (with IF NOT EXISTS, parameter placeholders), UPDATE (with SET arithmetic, REMOVE, nested paths), DELETE. WHERE supports BETWEEN, IN, CONTAINS, IS MISSING, IS NOT MISSING, AND, OR, NOT, parenthesised grouping up to 64 levels deep, and nested paths; AND binds tighter than OR, and a NOT over a group is applied by De Morgan. An index is named in the FROM clause as "table"."index", which serves the read from that GSI or LSI on SELECT only; a write statement rejects the qualifier.
